methods.label: Shift the floor by an integer
methods.explanation:
Subtracting an integer shifts the floor by that same integer. To see this here, let \(n=\lfloor x\rfloor\). Then
\[
n\le x<n+1,
\]
so subtracting \(2\) gives \(n-2\le x-2<n-1\). Hence \(\lfloor x-2\rfloor=n-2\).

The two expressions for \(y\) must agree, giving
\[
2n+3=3(n-2)+5=3n-1.
\]
Thus \(n=4\), and \(y=2(4)+3=11\). Since \(\lfloor x\rfloor=4\), we have \(4\le x<5\). The condition that \(x\) is not an integer removes the endpoint \(x=4\), leaving \(4<x<5\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{15<x+y<16}.
\]
Conversely, every \(x\) in \((4,5)\), together with \(y=11\), satisfies both original equations, so this is the full range. The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
